title: The Rogue Planet That 'Carries' an Ocean of Boiling Mercury
hook: A planet with seas of liquid mercury, hurtling through the galaxy at 1 million mph — and it's on a collision course with our solar system's edge.
why_this_can_go_viral: Visceral imagery of boiling metal oceans paired with an imminent threat triggers fear and awe — perfect for shareable cosmic horror content.

title: The Dark Matter 'Web' That's Strangling a Galaxy from the Inside
hook: Astronomers discovered a galaxy where dark matter has woven itself into a net — and it's slowly choking off all its star formation.
why_this_can_go_viral: The metaphor of a 'strangling web' is highly visual and terrifying — dark matter becomes a predator, not just a mystery.

title: The Declassified KGB File: 'We Found a Portal at the Edge of the Solar System'
hook: A Soviet probe sent back data showing a tear in spacetime beyond Pluto — then went silent the moment it crossed through.
why_this_can_go_viral: Classified Soviet documents + a literal portal at the edge of our system — conspiracists and sci-fi fans will share this instantly.

title: The Stellar Danger: A Star That 'Bleeds' Plasma That Burns at 100,000 Degrees
hook: A star with wounds that spew plasma streams hotter than its core — one of those streams is pointed directly at a nearby planetary system.
why_this_can_go_viral: The image of a 'bleeding' star is grotesque and memorable — makes stellar physics feel alive and threatening.

title: The Astronomical Anomaly: A Star That Orbits Something Invisible — And It's Accelerating
hook: A star is orbiting an empty patch of space, and its orbit is getting faster — whatever's there is pulling it in, and it's completely black.
why_this_can_go_viral: The mystery of something invisible that accelerates a star's orbit is pure 'what the hell is that?' content — drives engagement.

title: The Declassified CIA File: 'We Tracked an Asteroid That Changed Course — On Its Own'
hook: An asteroid made a sharp turn in deep space, not due to gravity — the CIA tracked it for years before it vanished behind the Moon.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of a non-gravitational asteroid course change screams 'alien technology' — CIA involvement adds conspiratorial heat.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Copies' Every Message We Send It — Then Speeds It Up
hook: A repeating signal from 4 light-years away doesn't just echo — it copies our transmissions and plays them back at increasingly faster speeds.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea of an alien 'mimic' that learns and accelerates is deeply unsettling — feels like the start of a horror movie.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came from a Supernova That Hit Earth Twice'
hook: A supernova 800 light-years away sent two radiation pulses — one missed, the second will arrive in 50 years. It already wiped out a species before.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'second strike' narrative is terrifying and urgent — viewers will feel like Earth is in a cosmic crossfire.

title: The Declassified DARPA File: 'We Created a Star in a Lab — It Started Sending Signals'
hook: DARPA's miniaturized fusion experiment produced a stable star for 12 seconds — then it began emitting a rhythmic pulse that matched no known physics.
why_this_can_go_viral: Humans creating a star that then 'talks' back is the ultimate playing-god narrative — conspiracists and science fans unite.

title: The Rogue Planet That 'Traps' Light in Its Atmosphere — It's Invisible to Telescopes
hook: A planet with an atmosphere so dense it traps all light — we only know it exists because it swallowed a comet and we heard the crunch.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'crunch' detail is viscerally satisfying — an invisible world revealed by sound is a rare and creepy concept.

title: The Stellar Danger: A Neutron Star That 'Spins' at 716 Times Per Second — And It's Wobbling
hook: The fastest-spinning object in the universe is wobbling, and every wobble sends a jet of radiation that could sterilize a galaxy.
why_this_can_go_viral: The combination of extreme speed and instability creates a ticking-bomb narrative that's hard to look away from.

title: The Declassified Soviet File: 'We Detected a Cosmic Wall Made of Ice'
hook: A Soviet telescope found a structure at the edge of the Kuiper Belt — a wall of crystalline ice, perfectly smooth, extending for billions of miles.
why_this_can_go_viral: The 'ice wall at the edge of the solar system' plays into flat Earth conspiracy with actual science — viral gold.

title: The Dark Matter 'Vortex' That's Pulling Our Solar System Off Course
hook: Our solar system is drifting faster than expected — a dark matter vortex 500 light-years wide is tugging us toward a region of empty space.
why_this_can_go_viral: The idea that we're being 'pulled' by an invisible force taps into deep existential dread — feels like we're not in control.

title: The Strange Cosmic Signal That 'Travels' Faster Than Light — And We Tracked Its Source
hook: A signal that breaks causality — it arrived before it was sent. We traced it to a dead star that shouldn't be able to transmit anything.
why_this_can_go_viral: Breaking causality is a mind-bending concept — viewers will argue about time travel and alien tech in the comments.

title: The Extinction Event That 'Came from a Comet That Was a Dead Alien Probe'
hook: A comet that struck Earth 12,000 years ago wasn't ice and rock — it was a hollow shell containing an alien navigation system, still active.
why_this_can_go_viral: Ancient alien probe embedded in an extinction event is two viral concepts in one — archaeologists and ufologists will fight over it.

title: The Declassified NASA File: 'We Found a Star That's Crying Liquid Helium'
hook: A star in the Andromeda galaxy is shedding tears of liquid helium — and the crying pattern matches the frequency of a human grieving ritual.
why_this_can_go_viral: Anthropomorphic grief on a cosmic scale is deeply poetic and sad — viewers will get emotional and share for the 'feels' factor.

title: The Rogue Black Hole That 'Eats' Dark Matter — And It's Growing Faster Than It Should
hook: A black hole consuming dark matter at an impossible rate — it's doubling in mass every 10 years and no one knows where it gets its fuel.
why_this_can_go_viral: A black hole with an 'unlimited' food source is terrifying — viewers will speculate about what happens when it runs out of fuel.

title: The Astronomical Anomaly: A Galaxy That Emits 'Bioluminescent' Light — Like a Living Organism
hook: A galaxy pulses with blue-green light in waves, exactly like bioluminescent plankton on Earth. Astronomers call it 'the Jellyfish Galaxy'.
why_this_can_go_viral: The comparison to living organisms makes the universe feel alive — viewers will wonder if galaxies are sentient.

title: The Fermi Paradox Answer: They're 'Hidden' in a Place We Never Thought to Look — Inside Stars
hook: What if advanced civilizations don't build Dyson spheres — they live inside stars, shielded from the universe, and we've been looking in the wrong place.
why_this_can_go_viral: The inside-of-a-star concept is completely novel — viewers will be obsessed with how such a civilization could exist.
